title: Stop the audit sender from losing events

blocks.text: The account service records an audit event for every sensitive action. Each request thread has an `AuditRecorder` that collects its events into batches and puts every full batch on an outbox queue; a sender thread takes batches from the outbox and ships them to the archive. Since the last release, which cut the recorder's allocations, the archive is missing most events, holds some of them twice, and the sender logs `ConcurrentModificationException` every few seconds.

Finish `handOff()` in `src/main/java/practice/AuditRecorder.java`. When you're done, every event a recorder records reaches the sender exactly once, in the batch it was recorded in, no matter how far the recorder has got by the time the sender takes that batch. About two lines.
The tests record on one thread and take batches from the outbox on another.

cases.says: every recorded event is handed over once, in order, in batches of the configured size with the rest in a last batch
a batch the sender takes from the outbox still holds the events it held when it was handed over, after the recorder has gone on recording

origin.section: The Edge Covers Writes Made Before the Release, Not After It

concepts: The edge covers writes made before the release; data changed after a put, a countDown or a submit is shared with no edge, so the producer must not touch it again.
